# OS command built from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/command-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) that
reaches a command the server starts with `System.Diagnostics.Process`:

- as the program itself: the file name given to `Process.Start`, to a `ProcessStartInfo`
  constructor or initializer, or assigned to `FileName` (also `process.StartInfo.FileName`);
- in the command line of a shell (`cmd`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh` and other POSIX shells, `pwsh`,
  `powershell`): an arguments string that holds a command switch (`/c`, `/k`, `-c`, `-Command`,
  `-EncodedCommand`) or is built elsewhere, and in an argument vector or `ArgumentList` the element
  that the shell runs as code (the script after `-c`, everything after `/c` or `-Command`).

Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and Minimal API
handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files, the body stream, and any
parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or
`[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and the request object itself (`Request.Query`,
`Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Path`, `QueryString`, `Body`, `ReadFormAsync()`,
`ReadFromJsonAsync()`). Numbers, booleans, GUIDs, dates and enums declared earlier in the file are
not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A shell treats `&`, `|`, `;`, `$(...)` and quotes in its command line as syntax. A value such as
`example.com & del /q C:\data` given to `cmd /c ping ...` runs a second command with the rights of
the web application. Letting the request choose the program is worse still: it can start any
program on the server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the host name is pasted into a command line that `cmd.exe` runs.

```csharp
using System.Diagnostics;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class NetworkController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet("ping")]
    public IActionResult Ping([FromQuery] string host)
    {
        using var process = Process.Start("cmd.exe", "/c ping -n 1 " + host);
        process.WaitForExit();
        return Ok(process.ExitCode);
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** `ping` runs without a shell and the host name is one argument of it.

```csharp
using System.Diagnostics;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class NetworkController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet("ping")]
    public IActionResult Ping([FromQuery] string host)
    {
        var info = new ProcessStartInfo("ping");
        info.ArgumentList.Add("-n");
        info.ArgumentList.Add("1");
        info.ArgumentList.Add(host);
        using var process = Process.Start(info);
        process!.WaitForExit();
        return Ok(process.ExitCode);
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Start the program directly, not through `cmd`, `sh` or PowerShell, and pass each value as its
  own argument: `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` or `Process.Start(fileName, arguments)` with an
  `IEnumerable<string>`, which .NET escapes for you.
- Keep the program fixed. If the request picks an action, map it to a fixed command with a
  lookup in a `static readonly` table of literals, or check it against a `static readonly` set of
  allowed values before use.
- If a shell is unavoidable, pass request data to the script as a positional parameter
  (`sh -c 'grep -- "$1" file' sh <value>`) instead of building it into the script text, and
  validate it first (convert numbers with `int.Parse`).
- Also check options: a value that starts with `-` can still change what a fixed program does
  (argument injection, which this rule does not report).
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages
- System.Diagnostics.Process

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
Under `qualor dotnet end`, Qualor's Roslyn taint engine runs this rule in OpenGrep's place, on the
projects the build compiled. It follows request data across methods, files and projects, through
properties, expression-bodied members and services registered for dependency injection, and into the
code of compiled Razor views and pages (`.cshtml`), and it reads all C# the compiler accepts. A
finding is of high confidence, or medium ("Possible" in Qualor) when its path goes through data
stored earlier in the request, a lookup by a request key, or a call or view the engine could not
narrow down. The engine's own limits are listed in the [models' README](../../../models/README.md),
section "Known limits". The bullets below are the OpenGrep rule's: it runs outside
`qualor dotnet end`, on C# files no compiled project covers, and as the fallback when the engine
cannot finish.

- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files. Request data read
  inside an expression-bodied method (`=> ...`) or a property getter
  (`string Tool => Request.Headers["X-Tool"]`) is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class (`Handlers.Run`) is
  missed. A controller named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check
  (`if (cmd != "uptime") return ...;`) or `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method
  does not, and a variable assigned again after a check still counts as checked.
- Argument injection into a fixed program that is not a shell (CWE-88) is not reported.
- A shell is recognised by its name written as a string literal, in place, in a constant or in a
  local variable, or as both branches of a ternary in a `ProcessStartInfo` initializer; a shell
  chosen by a ternary given to `Process.Start`, or read from configuration, is missed.
- An arguments string given to a POSIX shell is reported as a whole, so request data placed after
  the script (a positional parameter) is reported too; so is request data anywhere in an argument
  list that is built in a variable before it is passed.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/command/command-injection.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/command/command-injection.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
